messages:
sam: Quick Q — we're hitting ambiguous matches in staging when host+path+header rules overlap. What should be the canonical precedence order?
anika: My vote: evaluate host first (exact > wildcard), then path specificity (longest literal match), then header predicates. Header-based canaries should be able to override lower-specificity rules. :thinking:
matt: Agree on host->path prefiltering. Runtime note: we should avoid evaluating headers for every route, do it only on a small candidate set.
jose: Proposal I sketched: compute a specificity score: host_score + path_score + header_score. Example weights: exact host=100, wildcard host=50, path_score=number of literal segments * 10, header_predicate=+30 per predicate. Higher score wins. Tie-breaker = created_at asc.
tori: Hmm I worry about header_score being too strong — header-based rollouts should override in some cases but not trump a very specific path. Maybe header_score should be additive but smaller (e.g., +15) and multiple header conditions add up.
sam: Example to sanity-check:
```
routes:
  - id: r1
    host: api.redwood.com
    path: /v1/payments/*
    headers:
      x-canary: 'true'
    service: payments-v2
  - id: r2
    host: "*.redwood.com"
    path: /v1/*
    service: payments
```
R1 should win for requests to api.redwood.com with x-canary:true even though r2 is a wildcard host.
anika: Exactly. In score terms r1: host(100)+path(20)+header(15)=135 vs r2: host(50)+path(20)=70 -> r1 wins.
matt: Implementation idea: two-phase matching: 1) host index -> path trie -> shortlist (<=8 routes) 2) evaluate header predicates and final scoring. This keeps per-request cost low.
jose: Also we need to address weighted traffic (percent rolls). Suggest separation: header predicates are absolute filters applied first; for leftover traffic, we run weighted routing. So precedence: header override > weighted assignment > fallback rules.
tori: UX ask: console should show "Match reason" with the breakdown (host, path, header bits) and which predicate triggered. Ops needs that when troubleshooting misroutes.
anika: We'll also add telemetry counters for header-based matches and collisions so we can surface hotspots (e.g., many routes sharing same host+path but varying headers).
deploy-bot: Note: if you change precedence, remember to add migration doc for existing route configs.
sam: Action items: @anika to draft spec + example configs + unit tests; @matt to prototype trie+shortlist perf; @jose to add telemetry counters. I'll follow up with a design PR.
anika: I'll open the PR today, include tie-breaker rules and console wireframes.
matt: sgtm.
sam: Thanks all :heart:
